edges.ref: 44. Crawford JM, Baker AB. Experimental results on the application of satisfiability algorithms to scheduling problems. AAAI'94:1092-1097.

edges.target: 1990s local-search variants (GSAT, WalkSAT, GRASP, Iterated LS)
edges.ref: 18. Selman, Levesque, Mitchell AAAI'92; 19. Selman, Kautz, Cohen AAAI'94; 20. Feo & Resende JGO 1995; 21. Lourenco, Martin, Stutzle 2003

edges.target: Sawilowsky 0.35 sigma effect-size threshold
edges.ref: 48. Sawilowsky SS. New effect size rules of thumb. Journal of modern applied statistical methods. 2009;8(2):26.
edges.evidence: Differences smaller than Sawilowsky's threshold of 0.35 sigma 48 are clamped to zero before scoring.

edges.target: Welford's incremental mean/variance algorithm
edges.ref: 34. Welford BP. Note on a Method for Calculating Corrected Sums of Squares and Products. Technometrics. 1962;4(3):419-420.
edges.evidence: For Num, it updates mu, m2, and sd via Welford's algorithm 34, an exact and incremental method for updating mean and standard deviation.

edges.target: Irwin-Hall Gaussian approximation sampler (Johnson, Kotz & Balakrishnan)
edges.ref: 43. Johnson NL, Kotz S, Balakrishnan N. Continuous Univariate Distributions, Volume 2. Wiley. 2nd ed., 1995. Section 26.9.
edges.evidence: To pick from Nums, we draw from a distribution centered on a supplied mu (defaulting to the column mean) using the Irwin-Hall sampler 43.

edges.target: Reference-optimum convention (McGeoch; Cohen)
edges.ref: 47. McGeoch CC. A Guide to Experimental Algorithmics. Cambridge University Press, 2012 / 29. Cohen PR. Empirical methods for artificial intelligence. MIT Press, 1995.
edges.evidence: According to the empirical algorithms literature 47,29, the reference optimum is the best solution observed in the dataset.

edges.target: Cohen straw-man baseline methodology
edges.ref: 29. Cohen PR. Empirical methods for artificial intelligence. MIT press Cambridge, MA, 1995.
edges.evidence: Cohen 29 argued that supposedly sophisticated methods should always be benchmarked against seemingly stupider ones, the 'straw man' approach to scientific verification.

edges.target: Surrogate NAS benchmark protocol (Zela et al.)

edges.target: k-means++ seeding (Arthur & Vassilvitskii)
edges.ref: 42. Arthur D, Vassilvitskii S. k-means++: The Advantages of Careful Seeding. SODA '07:1027-1035.
edges.evidence: k-means++ 42 is a heuristic for picking the initial clusters given to k-means. The heuristic picks one centroid at random, then picks each subsequent centroid with probability proportional to its squared distance

edges.target: Aha's instance-based distance heuristics (Aha, Kibler & Albert)

edges.evidence: The per-column distance is aha (after Aha's 1991 instance-based reasoning algorithm 41) ... If both values are missing, their distance is maximal (Aha's heuristic).

edges.target: No-Free-Lunch theorem (Wolpert & Macready)

edges.evidence: as per the No-Free-Lunch theorem 82 (no learner dominates universally) we make no such claim for EZR. Rather, we frame EZR as a strong, simple baseline

not_reuse_examples: Arcuri & Briand [88]: named only as a 'future extension' for effect-size reporting; not applied.
Wilcoxon / Cliff's delta: explicitly NOT used (pre-registered 0.35 sigma clamp instead); no statmethod edge.
Settles [60,70], Zhu [69], Pearson [65], Chang [66]: qualitative history of feature selection / active learning; no number or theorem applied.
Witten & Frank [40], PEP 544/557 [37,38], Lewis et al. RAG [75], Easterby-Smith/Kington/Valerdi [49-51], Wu/Kang/Shepperd/Kamei [53-56], Yu Q [76]: framing/background only.
Fu/Nair/Agrawal/Tantithamthavorn/Grinsztajn/Hou 'simpler beats complex' papers [30-33,89-91]: cited as precedent for the thesis, not reused.
notes: Own-toolkit paper: 18 dataset edges (16 transitive via MOOT/Yu corpora), no third-party software executed; SMAC3/SHAP/LIME/ReliefF comparisons imported from self-papers [6,25] (executed=false); fresh experiments are SA-vs-LS (refutes 1990s LS literature) and a CNB re-run of Yu's FASTREAD SLR study (replication, refutes Yu's recall-only protocol and Rennie's normalization); all v1 sanitychecks except Tempero retyped to numericfact.
